description:
Third hang path, found by dogfooding while fixing bd-95p. NOT fixed there —
bd-95p stopped `bn sync` from hanging, but the underlying stall is still real.

Measured against a black-hole IP (10.255.255.1): `sync_in_progress` stayed TRUE
for ~130 SECONDS — the kernel's TCP connect timeout — before finally erroring
with "failed to fetch from remote".

Location: crates/kopi-beans/src/git/gix_compat.rs:926,
    prepare.receive(gix::progress::Discard, &interrupt)

The interesting part: there IS already an `AtomicBool` interrupt flag right
there at line 924. Nothing ever sets it from a timer. So the mechanism to abort
a stalled fetch is ALREADY WIRED UP and simply never fired. Should be a small
fix — spawn a watchdog that flips the flag at a deadline.

Note the asymmetry this leaves us with, which is why it deserves fixing rather
than shrugging at:
  * PUSH now has a watchdog (bd-95p): process deadline + git-native
    http.lowSpeedLimit/lowSpeedTime.
  * FETCH has neither. A stalled fetch still pins the lane for ~130s.

User-visible consequence even after bd-95p: `bn sync` returns promptly and
honestly says `sync in progress: true`, so nobody is stuck at the CLI — but the
daemon lane really is blocked for those ~130s, so the sync genuinely does not
progress and any waiter behind it just gets told to try again.

Use the same deadline reasoning as bd-95p's push watchdog and cross-reference
the constants so the two sides stay consistent.
title: kopi-beans: the FETCH side has no deadline either (~130s TCP stall keeps sync_in_progress true)
